Recent model runs have reinforced this scenario, reducing the chance of brief clearing that could allow readings to reach 30 °C or higher. Traders are weighting the high likelihood of persistent moisture and reduced insolation over the next 24 hours, with final resolution depending on verified observations from Shanghai’s official stations.

eventMetadata.context_description: **A building high-pressure ridge over western Europe is driving southerly warm-air advection and strong daytime heating, positioning Amsterdam for peak temperatures in the low-to-mid 30s Celsius on August 14, 2026.** Official short-range guidance from the KNMI, Met Office, and ECMWF ensembles currently clusters daily maxima around 32–33 °C, with some inland or southeastern locations reaching 35 °C, consistent with the market’s heaviest trading on 32 °C, 33 °C, and 34 °C outcomes. This represents roughly 10 °C above the long-term August climatological average high of ~21–22 °C and forms part of the Netherlands’ fifth heatwave of the season, with KNMI heat warnings already issued for Thursday and Friday. Abundant sunshine and a deep boundary layer support the elevated readings, while minor model spread arises from the precise timing of any late-day sea-breeze influence or residual cloud cover. Updated model runs and observational data through the next 24–48 hours will refine these probabilities ahead of official verification.
